documents.unit: Center for Innovation in Teaching & Learning (CITL)
documents.title: Integrate AI into your Teaching
documents.summary: The campus teaching center's page argues that faculty and students should engage with generative AI, lists benefits and ethical cautions (accuracy, privacy, access), and advises instructors to write specific syllabus language rather than a blanket policy. It also proposes assignment redesigns and points to college-level sample statements.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no campus rule on AI use. It says "The knee-jerk response is to add a blanket AI policy to your syllabus, but this is not advised" and tells instructors to "Define clear boundaries for AI use in course assignments and assessments", which hands the decision to instructors.

units.fit_note: Frames engagement with AI as modelling for students, not only learning the tool before setting policy.

documents.summary: Grainger offers four copy-and-adapt syllabus statements from a full ban to open use, plus example statements from CS 411 and Northern Illinois University. Instructors choose the tier and fill in the permitted and prohibited uses.
documents.stance_why: The page offers templates headed "Restricted", "Limited Use", "Use When Instructed to Do So" and "All Use" and does not choose one; the instructor picks, and the Limited Use template says "Add acceptable uses here".

units.why: The page "Template Statements for Engineering" offers four named statements (Restricted, Limited Use, Use When Instructed to Do So, All Use), so P05 (named tiers).
units.anchor: Template Statements for Engineering
units.policy: Template statements for engineering instructors are offered at four levels: Restricted, Limited Use, Use When Instructed to Do So, and All Use.

documents.title: Using AI
documents.summary: A Grainger guidance page sorting AI uses for teaching and learning into appropriate and inappropriate examples, with a test of whether AI augments or replaces thinking. It covers proofreading, course materials, tutoring, privacy, grading, peer review and homework.
documents.stance_why: The page does not hand the decision to instructors or ban AI; it says "If the intention of using AI is to augment human thinking, then it is likely an appropriate use of AI" and lists many appropriate uses with cautions, which is permission with conditions.

units.why: "If the intention of using AI is to replace human thinking, then it is likely an inappropriate use" is the converse of the test, P32, should-not.
